recipes.name: Acini di Pepe Salad
ingredients_raw: 1 (20 ounce) can crushed pineapple, drained with juice reserved
1 (15 ounce) can mandarin oranges, drained with liquid reserved
1 (8 ounce) container frozen whipped topping, thawed

steps.text: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Cook pasta in boiling water until tender yet firm to the bite, 8 to 10 minutes. Drain and set aside.

Combine reserved liquids from pineapple and oranges (about 1 1/2 cups), sugar, beaten eggs, flour, and salt in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Cook until thick, stirring constantly. Mix in cooked pasta. Refrigerate for 8 hours to overnight.
Transfer chilled pasta mixture to a large serving bowl. Stir in pineapple, oranges, whipped topping, and marshmallows. Top with cherries. Keep salad chilled in the refrigerator until serving time.

raw_recipe.headline: Acini di Pepe Salad
raw_recipe.description: Acini di pepe are marinated in a fruity custard and tossed with pineapple, oranges, whipped topping, and marshmallows for a bright, refreshing salad.

review.reviewBody: I have made this salad with a few alterations that make this recipe the bomb! Substitute the flour, and use 1 heaping tablespoon of corn starch. Once the pasta and the liquid mixture have been made wait until custardy mixture and pasta cool to room temperature. Once custard is room temperature add in the whip topping, until thouroughly blended. Then add the marshmellows, pasta, pineapple and mandarin oranges. I omit the cherries altogether. Whalla, I much better way of combining this salad with creamier results! :)

I have been making this salad for years and it is a favorite at family gatherings. I use a scant 1/2 cup sugar and 1 cup heavy cream instead of the frozen stuff. You won't believe the difference it makes! I also omit the cherries and add 2 cups red and/or green grapes, cut in half. I have always used pineapple tidbits as it gives the salad more texture. Note: using colored marshmallows would totally change the flavor of the salad and not in a good way!

I added diced mangoes, red and green grapes cut in half, and added fruit colored Marshmallows in plain yogurt refrigerated overnight. I also used real whipping cream. It was very good and very Eastery. Yes it made a lot but at the end of the day only a few servings were left.

I love this little dish. My family makes it at holidays. I used real whipping cream and added raspberries and blueberries. I also use about half of the crushed pineapple and it cuts back on the sweetness and stringy chunks.
I make this every holiday. And again today. Perfect just the way it is, but I also add a can of mixed fruit from heavy syrup. (Drained) Yum... Happy Memorial Day weekend all. ❤️

My mom has been making this since I was a kid. I recently made it for my baby shower, using the colored mini marshmallows and stirring the maraschino cherries (halved) in. It had a nice pastel color to it and my mother-in-law now requests it at every holiday meal! Great recipe! (P.S. I've also tried adding a can of tropical fruit salad that I slightly blitzed in the food processor, and it turned out really well)

I have been making this for years and people always request me to bring it. I am making it today for a huge family reunion tomorrow. Sometimes I will throw in a couple cans of drained fruit cocktail or tropical fruit. Never have added coconut. You must refrigerate overnight the pasta and sauce. Quit using cool whip because of the nasty they put in it. I use heavy whip cream now and it is delicious. Much better in my opinion. I keep 1/3 of it set aside and do not add marshmallows to that bowl for those who do not like that much sweetness. The rest I add the colored marshmallows to. The kids love that one. We also have to keep some at home because there is never any left to take back home.

I liked the concept of this salad but I thought it would be too sweet with whipped topping and marshmallows. I omitted the marshmallows and used sour cream instead of the whipped topping. Yum. I bet it would taste just as good if it was mixed with a nice creamy greek yogurt.

This was good, but for my taste there was too much whipped topping. I only added about 6oz. and that was too much. I also left out the marshmallows since I don't care for them and I substituted grapes for the cherries. If I do make this again, I think I'll only use 4 oz. of the whipped topping and see if I like it better. Or I might use real whipped cream.

This is a family favorite of ours. I always chill the pasta and liquid mixture several hours or overnight then add the whipped topping, marshmellows and fruit. The cherries are a bit too much, so I just add the pineapple and oranges.
mandarine instead of cherries !! good recipe! it is a keeper!!

I doubled it for a potluck and honestly, the single recipe would’ve been plenty. It was good and felt like a retro recipe! I couldn’t tell it had pasta as a main ingredient when I ate it. It just felt like a basic ambrosia salad. Thanks for the recipe! :)
Family loved it. Requested it again. Will definitely make again. Great for pot luck.
It was very good. I did only put a 1/2 cup of sugar in it, i would make it again.

I made recipe as listed and it was a hit. Many asked me to make for our next family
Get together and make double the amt.
My mother made this recipe over 20 years ago. It is the same thing! My whole family loved it!
I omitted the coconut but other than that ...this was a huge hit and it made enough for leftovers.

My mother used to make this and I haven't thought about it in years until I came across it on allrecipes. It was always a hit at family gatherings and parties. After seeing it on this site, I just had to make it to bring back the old memories. It was exactly like mom used to make. I gave it four stars because it's my personal opinion on the taste. But in fairness, everyone seems to love it.
